Plumbing, drainage & gas.

Identify which system is affected.

We define the affected service before arranging plumbing work. A leaking fitting, loss of hot water and repeated drainage overflow require different investigation. We separate finding the fault from the final repair and agree the shutdown and access arrangements with the people operating the property.

01 / Outdoor paved area affected by drainage planning

Identify which service is affected

Record whether water appears only when a particular fixture drains, during rain, or while the supply remains pressurised. Separate that evidence from the final repair scope. On occupied sites, agree who can confirm shut-off and restore each affected fixture or area.

For a recurring blockage, we ask which fixtures are affected, whether smells or slow discharge appear after particular activities and where inspection access can be provided. Supply shutdown, wastewater checks and any gas work are separately scoped with the responsible trade.

We compare when a ground inlet ponds with rainfall, irrigation and nearby plumbing use. Water backing up at several inlets suggests checking the shared downstream route. Ponding beside a clear inlet can point to paving levels. We list clearing and local repairs separately from alterations to the drainage route and agree how the affected area can be accessed.

  • Water supply and fittings

    We record the leaking point, affected fixtures and when the problem occurs. Accessible valves, connections and surrounding damage help define investigation and the parts to be considered.

  • Hot water

    We review the equipment information, affected outlets and reported changes in supply. A local fixture problem and an equipment or wider supply issue should not be priced as the same repair.

  • Wastewater and rainwater drainage

    We identify whether the issue occurs at one fixture, several connected points or an external drainage area. Timing during rain or normal use helps direct the investigation.

02 / Fixture access in a trading venue

Match parts to the existing installation

  • Pipework and equipment

    We check available pipe, valve and equipment details before ordering parts. Location, connection type and service access affect what can be repaired locally and what needs a wider change.

  • Gas work

    Gas service or equipment work is defined for the specific premises. We identify the equipment, required attendance and relevant records separately rather than treating it as an automatic addition to every plumbing visit.

Plan the interruption and the return to use

For example, a slow basin and water appearing at a floor waste are different observations. Record exactly which fixtures were being used and whether the floor was recently washed, then arrange access for the appropriate trade.

We record the branch or fixture affected, what other fixtures are served, and who can authorise an outage. We keep downstream drainage faults, water supply faults and gas work as separate entries so the appropriate trade can confirm its scope and any checks before the area reopens.

  1. 01

    Review the fault and access

    We confirm the affected areas, available records, inspection points and any further investigation needed before a repair can be settled.

  2. 02

    Coordinate the work

    We agree the affected facilities and shutdown window, protect surrounding finishes and carry out the confirmed work. Additional findings are recorded for a separate decision.

  3. 03

    Check operation

    We complete the relevant operating, leakage or drainage checks for the work performed and record what has been returned to use.

What changes the scope and cost

  • Visible and concealed conditions

    Accessible defects can be scoped differently from buried or concealed faults. Investigation, opening-up and reinstatement are identified where required.

  • Operations and materials

    Parts availability, affected outlets, shutdown arrangements, access and the work needed around the pipework all influence the quotation.

Confirm what can go back into use.

We record the investigation points, agreed checks and any areas that need a further visit before wall or paving reinstatement.

Useful records for the next maintenance decision

We record the repaired location, agreed parts and checks, together with any unresolved issue or further investigation. For recurring faults, a clear history helps distinguish a new event from an item already investigated, rather than repeating the same unclear instruction.

Before the visit we agree shut-off windows and alternative facilities if needed. After work we record the affected points, the agreed operational checks and any monitoring or further investigation required.

  • Affected fixture and timing
  • Agreed shut-off window
  • Checks and outstanding investigation
Prepare an enquiry ↗

Common questions

Can a recurring blockage simply be cleared again?
Record where the fault recurs, what it affects and prior repair work. Define repairs against the findings.
Do you quote the investigation separately?
For concealed faults, define the inspection scope first, then list parts, access and reinstatement based on the findings.
What should a hotel or café tell you before attendance?
Tell us which facilities are affected, when the symptoms occur, operating hours and any available equipment records. We use that information to discuss access and the interruption to water or equipment.
What information helps you quote a drainage problem?
We use the property address, the affected fixtures or area, when the problem occurs and any available photos to plan the investigation. If the cause is concealed, we explain the investigation scope before quoting the final repair.
